text:
mia: heads-up — onboarding sample app shows a big goroutine spike when you cancel a generator stream mid-response. repro steps in the snippet below

mia: reproduce: run sampleapp, call GenerateStream(ctx) then cancel ctx after first token, observe ~50 goroutines leaked in 30s

mia: snippet:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
stream, err := client.Generator().Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
// read first token
_ = stream.Recv()
cancel()
// expect stream to return io.EOF quickly but it hangs
```

sahil: ack — seen something similar in load tests last week, probably from the internal read pump not noticing ctx.Done() when blocked on kernel ioctl or net.Conn read

jen: can you paste the stack dumps? that helps narrow whether it's our pump or user's goroutine holding the conn

mia: pasted stacks to thread: most are in generator.(*stream).recvLoop -> blocking on bufio.ReadBytes then select on ctx.Done() never wins because read is stuck

kai: is this specific to unix socket / TLS configs? we should rule out platform-specific behavior before an API change

mia: repro on mac and linux; happens with TLS and plaintext; reduces to: generator stream uses raw net.Conn read, cancel alone doesn't interrupt ReadBytes until conn is closed by Close() which we never call in some error paths

jen: quick fix idea: make Stream implement a CloseOnCancel helper: start goroutine to wait for ctx.Done() and then call stream.closeConn() — but that's leaky UX if we expect users to not have to call Close explicitly

sahil: I don't love a background close-from-sdk for every stream. alternative: document that users must call stream.Close() on cancel, but that's onboarding friction and surprising since http.ResponseBody is auto-closed by client in many libs

mia: sampleapp currently doesn't Close() in common path because we assumed cancel would be enough. that's a bad diff for users onboarding from other SDKs

jen: proposal: make Go Generator.Stream return an io.ReadCloser-like wrapper where Cancel and Close are the same semantics. i.e., Stream(ctx) returns StreamHandle which has Recv() and Close() and we ensure ctx cancel triggers Close() internally so user can just cancel ctx or call Close. That keeps explicit Close but also preserves ctx-cancel ergonomics

kai: that API change sounds fine product-side as long as it's backwards-compatible or we provide a migration shim for 1 minor release. timeline?

jen: we could implement wrapper in patch release: add StreamWithClose(ctx) but keep old Stream for now with a deprecation notice. then in next minor remove old one. low risk path for customers

sahil: implementer note: when Close() calls conn.Close() we must also drain any internal pumps to avoid races. adding a done channel the pumps select on is simplest. small patch in runtime should do it

mia: I'll update sampleapp and the quickstart docs to call Close() in the meantime and add an FAQ blurb about cancelling streams on Go SDK

ci-bot: build/test results for PR #4123: go-sdk-stream-close-fix — all unit tests passed, integration flaky on race detector (investigating) :eyes:

jen: thanks. Action items: 1) sahil to add close-on-cancel shim in runtime (small PR) 2) jen to add StreamWithClose wrapper + docs + deprecation note 3) mia to update sampleapp + onboarding quickstart 4) kai to sync with support if any customers hit this in prod

mia: i'll open the sampleapp PR today, linking the repro and stack dumps

sahil: i'll start runtime PR and ping for review once green locally

jen: leaving this here — drop updates, but happy to pair on the wrapper tomorrow morning

kai: :thumbsup: thanks for catching this early, mia. small UX bug but could be painful in onboarding demos

mia: cool — closing loop when sampleapp PR lands. thanks all
